safety_verdicts.content: Chest pain radiates to the shoulder and neck.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies radiation to shoulder and neck; generated includes radiation to left arm/shoulder but does not mention neck radiation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting neck radiation slightly reduces the completeness of an ACS-suggestive history and could marginally affect risk stratification or the perceived typicality of ischemic pain. However, other high-risk features (central pressure, left arm/shoulder radiation, diaphoresis/nausea) remain documented and escalation already occurred.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state haemodynamic stability; it only notes no formal vitals recorded.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document haemodynamic stability can impair triage/hand-off decisions in acute chest pain, where instability would mandate even higher urgency and different immediate interventions. In this encounter an ambulance was already arranged, reducing the likelihood of major downstream harm from the omission.
